clue.text: Only items of quality, every one for my pleasure

parts.note: if there is no tat (cheap junk) then everything is of quality: NO TAT
every one means all

explanation.surface: A collector insists on owning only the finest pieces, purely for personal enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for my pleasure' looks like the end of the collector's sentence; 'my pleasure' is the polite reply itself, with 'for' as a link. TAT is British slang for tasteless junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are polite replies when someone says thank you, so either can stand in for the other.

clue.text: Covered by maid, ledge gathering dust

indicators.note: the answer lies covered by the letters of the following words, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A ledge the maid never cleans sits thick with dust.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left gathering dust is unused, lying idle rather than being put to work.

clue.text: See 22 across
Humour, vacuous amusement in setting

indicators.note: in puts the shortened amusement into the setting

parts.note: a setting is a place, the scene where something happens

indicators.note: vacuous means emptied, so the word amusement keeps only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone tries to humour others with hollow entertainment in a particular setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humour' is a verb here, to indulge someone, not the noun for comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: To humour someone is to go along with their wishes to keep them happy, the same as appeasing them.

clue.text: Baltic Sea? No, it turns north

indicators.note: the letters of sea, no and it turn about into a new arrangement

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a stretch of water is the Baltic Sea, and is told no, it heads north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' rearranges SEANOIT into ESTONIA before N is added. 'Baltic' looks like part of the sea's name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is one of the three Baltic states, so a person or thing from there is Baltic.

clue.text: A little sign left in vault

indicators.note: in places the signing and the left inside the leap

parts.note: to vault is to leap or spring
to ink a deal is to sign it

explanation.surface: A small mark has been left inside a vault or crypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vault' reads as a burial chamber but is the verb, to leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinkling is a small, scattered amount, so 'a little' of something.

clue.text: Preacher's ecclesiastic weapon

indicators.note: a preacher speaks from the pulpit, so what follows is a word as it is spoken

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral

explanation.surface: A clergyman's preferred weapon is an odd thing to imagine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preacher's' signals speech: a cathedral CANON sounds the same as the big gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon is a large heavy gun, an artillery weapon.

clue.text: File case of overemotional guff

parts.note: a file is a folder for documents

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A dossier of sentimental twaddle is filed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Folderol is foolish talk or nonsense, the same as guff.

clue.text: Pigment good in water

indicators.note: in puts the good inside the water

parts.note: the sea is a body of water
PI, short for pious, is a crossword abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A fine pigment dissolved in water, as for a watercolour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown pigment, originally made from cuttlefish ink.

clue.text: See 24
New variation, including a hundred old pieces

indicators.note: including means the rearranged letters take the hundred inside them
something new is a fresh version, so the letters of variation are rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A fresh variation on a theme incorporates a hundred antique items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges VARIATION, and 'including' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoriana means objects from the Victorian era, collected now as antiques or old pieces.

clue.text: Fat queen in store …

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A plump queen is in a shop, leading into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a cool room or cupboard for storing food.

clue.text: Finished nursing little girl, cut

indicators.note: nursing means holding inside, as a nurse holds a baby

parts.note: to have done something is to have finished it: did
mini means small, little
she stands for any girl or woman

explanation.surface: Someone finished caring for a small girl and then cut her off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finished' gives the past tense DID, as in 'did the job'; 'girl' gives the pronoun, not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cut, as in reduced, has been diminished, made smaller.

clue.text: … very different partner in philosophy?

parts.note: the ellipsis follows on from 'Fat queen' in the previous clue; very different from fat is thin
the partner of a queen is a king

explanation.surface: A companion completely unlike the plump queen of the previous clue, presented as a matter of philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses join this clue to 12 across: the opposite of 'Fat queen' is a THIN KING. The question mark flags a loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Philosophy is a school of thought, and thinking is used the same way: current thinking on a subject.

clue.text: Metal once found in bottom of fruit?

indicators.note: of says the bottom belongs to the fruit, so the fruit comes first

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
bum is British slang for the bottom, the backside

explanation.surface: A piece of metal discovered at the bottom of a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: BUM is everyday British slang for the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbum is the Latin name for lead, an older term, which is why lead's symbol is Pb.

clue.text: Dizzy playing tunes on jazzy day

indicators.note: playing about with the letters of tunes rearranges them
jazzy suggests improvising freely, so the letters of day are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone feels lightheaded after playing tunes all through a lively day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' shuffles TUNES into UNSTE and 'jazzy' shuffles DAY into EADY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dizzy person is unsteady on their feet, wobbly and off balance.

clue.text: See 25
Running water options on craft, type of carrier

parts.note: taps are marked H and C, for hot and cold running water
art means craft, skill

explanation.surface: A boat offers hot and cold water, and a type of vessel carries it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'options' are the hot and cold taps, H AND C.
explanation.definitionFit: A handcart is a small cart pushed by hand, used to carry goods.

clue.text: Teacher in a flap upended coffee-maker

indicators.note: upended means turned upside down, so in a down clue the whole is read bottom to top
in puts the teacher inside the flap

parts.note: a tab is a small flap
schoolchildren call a male teacher sir

explanation.surface: A flustered teacher knocks over the coffee machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upended' turns A TSIRAB upward. 'in a flap' looks like flustered; here a flap is a tab.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista is the person who makes coffee in a café, so a coffee-maker in human form.

clue.text: Laxative one girl fed to another

indicators.note: fed to means put into, so one name goes inside the other

parts.note: Mia is another girl's name
Agnes is a girl's name

explanation.surface: One girl gives a laxative to another.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk of magnesia is a common laxative and antacid.

clue.text: How formula for poison is written in capital city

parts.words: How formula for poison is written
parts.note: arsenic, a poison, has the chemical formula As: an A then an S

explanation.surface: A question of how a poison's chemical formula is noted down in some capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as A THEN S, which is how As, the symbol for arsenic, is written.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece.

clue.text: One banked on needing loco — did one?

definitions.text: One banked on needing loco — did one?

indicators.note: in a down entry on means placed after, and RIVER runs down from 3
loco is slang for crazy, so the letters of needing go mad and rearrange

parts.note: a river is something with banks

explanation.surface: Someone was relied upon, needing a locomotive, and did they need one?
explanation.walkthrough: 'loco' (crazy) is the anagram signal, though it looks like a train. In this down light, 'on' puts the second part below the first. As a whole, someone who needs a loco is a train driver.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine driver drives a railway locomotive, so a loco is exactly what one needs.

clue.text: Little predatory bird, swallow biting leg off

indicators.note: biting means the swallowing word closes around the rest

parts.note: to swallow food is to eat it

indicators.note: off means gone bad, so the letters of leg are put out of order

explanation.surface: A swallow bites a leg off a small bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' looks like the bird but is the verb. 'off' scrambles LEG to AGL.
explanation.definitionFit: An eaglet is a young eagle, a small bird of prey.

clue.text: Serving as correction, speed of light accelerating

parts.note: c is the physics symbol for the speed of light
accelerating means hastening, speeding up

explanation.surface: A rebuke delivered at the speed of light, and getting faster.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastening experiences rebuke and humble someone, acting as a correction to their behaviour.

clue.text: Kick people out, event usually for children

parts.note: to kick staff out is to sack them; the out completes that phrase
a race is a people, a group sharing ancestry

explanation.surface: Throwing people out of an event that is usually meant for children.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack race is a school sports day event in which children hop along in sacks.

clue.text: Reportedly plant weed somewhere in London

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so what is heard counts, not the spelling

parts.note: to sow is to plant seeds, and to hoe is to weed; said together they make the answer

explanation.surface: Word has it that a weed has been planted somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: SOW HOE said aloud gives the London district; SOHO is a lively area of central London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of central London, famous for its nightlife and restaurants.

clue.text: Conclusion can't be reached — sigh!

parts.note: the word sigh is the word sight with its final letter, its end, missing

explanation.surface: Someone sighs at an argument that cannot be settled.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, the answer says SIGHT with no end, and SIGHT without its T is 'sigh', the clue's last word.
explanation.definitionFit: When there is no end in sight, a task or situation seems as if it will never finish.

clue.text: Piano piece, both grand and upright, thrashed out

definitions.text: Piano piece, both grand and upright

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of thrashed are rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of music played on a piano, both grand and upright, gets bashed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano' is the architect Renzo Piano, and grand and upright describe the building, not the instrument. THE SHARD is the tallest skyscraper in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shard is a London skyscraper designed by Renzo Piano, a tall and grand piece of his work.
